description: Predicates the lens specialists ask for, with precedents (proposals/predicate_needs.py; 39 §7). A request is a lead for the curator, never a registry change.

requests.name: defectedTo
definitions: A person or unit left one side for the opposing commander at a stated date.
A person or group leaves one side and goes over to another at a date.
A person or contingent abandons one side and goes over to the opposing leader at a given date.

evidence.example: Dellius defectedTo Augustus, shortly before 2 Sep 31 BCE
Quintus Dellius defectedTo Augustus, before 2 Sept 31 BCE
Gnaeus Domitius Ahenobarbus defectedTo Augustus, 31 BCE (before September)

shape.basis: The desertion is an act; the allegiance after it is a state (servedUnder, alliedWith with a start).
shape.by: Claude (proposed under D-138, 2026-11-12; for the curator to confirm)

requests.name: abandonedCommand
definitions: A commander leaves the force under his command while it is still engaged, at a given date.

evidence.example: Mark Antony abandonedCommand Antony's fleet at Actium, 2 September 31 BCE

evidence.quotation: Canidius their general had run away by night and forsaken the camp

shape.basis: Leaving a force mid-battle is an act (already depicted: Antony follows Cleopatra).
shape.by: Claude (proposed under D-138, 2026-11-12; for the curator to confirm)

requests.name: adoptedBy
definitions: An act: an adoption, in which one person took another as son, at a date (or by will, as Caesar's of Octavian); adopter and adoptee are roles. The new gens is an ofGens claim of its own (46).

evidence.ref: chats/Agents and Exploration.yml (ChatGPT review of the architecture, 2026-11-21); 39 §10, the families the lens run and the Gracchus narrative ask for. Octavian, a Julius by adoption, is the case doc 46 names.

legacy.name: ADOPTED_BY
legacy.description: Person was legally adopted by adopter

shape.basis: D-170: a lasting bond of parent and child in law, like childOf, with its form (adoptio, adrogatio, by will) as a role Type. Overrides the event shape proposed 2026-11-22 (48 §3).
shape.by: curator, 2026-11-22 (D-170, confirmed in chat)

requests.name: amicusOf
definitions: Two people were bound in amicitia, the Roman political friendship with its duties of support, over a time. Narrower than alliedWith (any alliance, of persons, groups or states).

evidence.ref: chats/Agents and Exploration.yml (ChatGPT review of the architecture, 2026-11-21); 39 §10, the families the lens run and the Gracchus narrative ask for. Whether amicitia needs its own predicate or alliedWith with a basis is the curator's choice (48 §3).

shape.basis: A bond held over time between two people, not an act.
shape.by: curator, 2026-11-22 (48 §3, confirmed in chat)

requests.name: captured
definitions: A force took enemy vessels or men in a given engagement on a given date.

evidence.example: Octavian's fleet at Actium captured 300 ships of Antony's fleet, 2 Sep 31 BCE (Plutarch)

shape.basis: A capture happens at a moment in an engagement, with captor and captured.
shape.by: Claude (proposed under D-138, 2026-11-12; for the curator to confirm)

requests.name: capturedAsBooty
definitions: A side took ships, treasure or goods from the enemy in an engagement at a given time.

evidence.example: Octavian's fleet at Actium capturedAsBooty ships of Antony's fleet at Actium, time -0030-09-02 (c251).

shape.basis: Taking booty is an act within an engagement.
shape.by: Claude (proposed under D-138, 2026-11-12; for the curator to confirm)

requests.name: claimedDivineAssociation
definitions: A person publicly associates himself or herself with a deity during a time span.

evidence.example: Augustus claimedDivineAssociation Apollo, -0036/-0027

shape.basis: An association with a deity is held over time.
shape.by: Claude (proposed under D-138, 2026-11-12; for the curator to confirm)

requests.name: commemorates
definitions: A foundation, monument, rite or work was made in order to keep the memory of an event.

evidence.example: Nicopolis (Place) commemorates Battle of Actium (Event), voiced by Strabo 7.7.6

shape.basis: A monument or rite stands in a lasting relation to the event it recalls.
shape.by: Claude (proposed under D-138, 2026-11-12; for the curator to confirm)

requests.name: conscriptedInto
definitions: Persons are compelled into service in a force at a given date.

evidence.example: Greek civilians conscriptedInto Antony's fleet at Actium, 31 BCE

shape.basis: A levy is an act of raising men.
shape.by: Claude (proposed under D-138, 2026-11-12; for the curator to confirm)

requests.name: declaredWarByRitual
definitions: A person or priestly college performs the ritual declaration of war against a named enemy at a date.

evidence.example: Augustus declaredWarByRitual Cleopatra, -0032

shape.basis: The fetial declaration is a ritual act.
shape.by: Claude (proposed under D-138, 2026-11-12; for the curator to confirm)

requests.name: declaredWarOn
definitions: A body or magistrate formally declares war on a person or polity at a date.

evidence.example: Roman Senate declaredWarOn Cleopatra, 32 BCE (phase: 'war declared on Cleopatra')

shape.basis: A declaration of war is a dated act by a body, often with a ritual and a place.
shape.by: Claude (proposed under D-138, 2026-11-12; for the curator to confirm)

requests.name: decreedThanksgiving
definitions: The Senate or another body decrees a supplicatio for a victory at a date.

evidence.example: Senate decreedThanksgiving Battle of Actium, -0030

shape.basis: A supplicatio is decreed on a date by a body.
shape.by: Claude (proposed under D-138, 2026-11-12; for the curator to confirm)

requests.name: dedicatedSpoils
definitions: A person consecrated captured goods or ships to a deity or sanctuary at a given time.

evidence.example: Augustus dedicatedSpoils captured ships to Apollo at Actium, time -0030 (c56, c368).

shape.basis: A dedication is a ceremony with a dedicator, an object, and a god.
shape.by: Claude (proposed under D-138, 2026-11-12; for the curator to confirm)

requests.name: dedicatedTo
definitions: A person dedicates an object (spoils, ships, building) to a deity at a given date.

evidence.example: Augustus dedicatedTo Apollo (captured ships), -0030

shape.basis: A dedication is an act with a date and a dedicator.
shape.by: Claude (proposed under D-138, 2026-11-12; for the curator to confirm)

requests.name: delegatedCommandTo
definitions: A holder of imperium assigned a deputy (legatus) to command a force or division for a stated period.

evidence.example: Augustus delegatedCommandTo Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa for the left wing of Octavian's fleet, 2 Sep 31 BCE

shape.basis: Delegated command holds between two people over a time.
shape.by: Claude (proposed under D-138, 2026-11-12; for the curator to confirm)

requests.name: deprivedOfPosition
definitions: A person is stripped of an office or designated office by a named body at a date.

evidence.example: Mark Antony deprivedOfPosition consulship (designate for 31 BCE), 32 BCE

legacy.name: POSITION_HELD
legacy.description: Person held a position or office

shape.basis: The end of a heldPosition claim, not a predicate of its own.
shape.by: Claude (proposed under D-138, 2026-11-12; for the curator to confirm)

requests.name: grantedClemencyTo
definitions: A victor spares a named opponent or group at a date.

evidence.example: Augustus grantedClemencyTo Gaius Sosius, after Sept 31 BCE

legacy.name: TITLE_GRANTED_BY
legacy.description: Person was granted title by grantor

shape.basis: Clemency is granted in an act.
shape.by: Claude (proposed under D-138, 2026-11-12; for the curator to confirm)

requests.name: hadStatus
definitions: A person holds a recognised standing (a status Type such as matrona) over a time, not an office and not a part played in an event.
requestedBy: curator (with Claude, 2026-11-13; README review item 3, Type categories)

evidence.ref: Wikidata observation of Fulvia's position held (P39): matrona; the heldPosition claim was rejected as malformed on 2026-11-12, because matrona is a status, not an office

shape.basis: A standing a person holds over time, between a person and a status Type; not an act.

requests.name: hadStrength
definitions: A force numbered a given count of ships or men at a given date, as stated by one source. It is reported per voice and never reconciled.

evidence.example: Cleopatra's squadron at Actium hadStrength 60 ships, 2 Sep 31 BCE (Plutarch; Hale)

shape.basis: A number on a claim (quantityMinimum, quantityMaximum).
shape.by: Claude (proposed under D-138, 2026-11-12; for the curator to confirm)

requests.name: informedBy
definitions: A source's account rests on a named person's report: the source says it had the story from them (an informant, often an eyewitness).

evidence.quotation: my great-grandfather Nicarchus used to tell how all his fellow-citizens were compelled to carry on their shoulders a stipulated measure of wheat down to the sea at Anticyra

cidoc.note: Information concept very broad in Wikidata

shape.basis: A standing relation between a source and the person its account rests on, not an act within the events it tells.

requests.name: instituted
definitions: A person founds recurring games, a festival or a cult at a date.

evidence.example: Augustus instituted Ludi Actiaci, c. -0029

shape.basis: Instituting a rite or games is a founding act.
shape.by: Claude (proposed under D-138, 2026-11-12; for the curator to confirm)

requests.name: intercededFor
definitions: A person pledges himself or pleads with a third party on behalf of another at a given date.

evidence.example: Lucius Arruntius intercededFor Gaius Sosius, 31 BCE

shape.basis: An intercession is an act.
shape.by: Claude (proposed under D-138, 2026-11-12; for the curator to confirm)

requests.name: leviedOn
definitions: A person or authority imposed a tax, levy or contribution on a group or place at a given time.

evidence.example: Augustus leviedOn citizens of Italy, time -0032 (Dio 50.10, to be read).

shape.basis: A levy or tax imposed is an act with several parties.
shape.by: Claude (proposed under D-138, 2026-11-12; for the curator to confirm)

requests.name: locatedAt
definitions: An object stands or is kept at a place (a monument on its site, an inscription in a city), over a time where known.
requestedBy: curator (with Claude, 2026-11-13; the Campsite Memorial of Augustus as an Object)

evidence.quotation: he dedicated the monument on the site of his headquarters
evidence.ref: Strauss, The War That Made the Roman Empire, p. 5 (the curator's transcription); the memorial's Wikidata record also gives coordinates (P625) near Nicopolis

legacy.name: LOCATED_IN
legacy.wikidata: P131 (located in the administrative territorial entity)

shape.basis: Where an object stands is a standing relation between an Object and a Place, not an act.

requests.name: patronOf
definitions: A person stood as patron to a client (a person, a town, or a community) over a time: the Roman bond of patrocinium and clientela, with obligations both ways. The client's side is the same claim read from the object.

evidence.ref: chats/Agents and Exploration.yml (ChatGPT review of the architecture, 2026-11-21); 39 §10, the families the lens run and the Gracchus narrative ask for. Patronage is the bond historians use to explain votes and support; no predicate holds it.

shape.basis: A bond held over time between two parties, not an act.
shape.by: curator, 2026-11-22 (48 §3, confirmed in chat)

requests.name: proposedLaw
definitions: An act: a magistrate brought a law before an assembly (rogatio), at a date; proposer, assembly and the law are roles, and the law's passage or rejection is the outcome (resultedIn).

evidence.ref: chats/Agents and Exploration.yml (ChatGPT review of the architecture, 2026-11-21); 39 §10, the families the lens run and the Gracchus narrative ask for. The objectKind Law waits on the Law kind (48 §4).

legacy.name: PROPOSED_BY
legacy.description: Node was proposed by this facet agent

shape.basis: A proposal is an act before an assembly with proposer and law as roles; passage is its outcome (D-138).
shape.by: curator, 2026-11-22 (48 §3, confirmed in chat)

requests.name: prosecuted
definitions: An act: a trial, in which one person charged another before a court, at a date; the accuser, defendant, presiding magistrate and verdict are roles and outcomes of the Event.

evidence.ref: chats/Agents and Exploration.yml (ChatGPT review of the architecture, 2026-11-21); 39 §10, the families the lens run and the Gracchus narrative ask for. Legal acts (charged, convicted, exiled, declared hostis) are a family 39 §10 lists.

shape.basis: A trial happens at a date with accuser, defendant and court: an Event with roles (D-138).
shape.by: curator, 2026-11-22 (48 §3, confirmed in chat)

requests.name: reportsOmen
definitions: A work reports an omen or portent concerning a person or event. The claim is attributed to the work, not asserted as having happened, and is time-boxed to the reported date.

evidence.example: Life of Antony reportsOmen (ass Eutychus) concerning Augustus, -0031

shape.basis: An omen is an occurrence a Work reports.
shape.by: Claude (proposed under D-138, 2026-11-12; for the curator to confirm)

requests.name: requisitionedFrom
definitions: A commander or army compulsorily took grain, materials, animals or labour from a community at a given time.

evidence.example: Mark Antony requisitionedFrom Chaeronea, time -0031 (Plutarch 68.4, to be read).

shape.basis: A requisition is an act with several parties.
shape.by: Claude (proposed under D-138, 2026-11-12; for the curator to confirm)

requests.name: settledAt
definitions: Discharged soldiers of a force were settled on land at a place at a stated date.

evidence.example: veterans of Octavian's forces settledAt colonies in Italy, 30 BCE onward (to be grounded in Dio 51.3-4 or Res Gestae 3.3)

shape.basis: Settling veterans is an act of distribution.
shape.by: Claude (proposed under D-138, 2026-11-12; for the curator to confirm)

requests.name: settledOn
definitions: A person or authority assigned land at a place to settlers or veterans at a given time.

evidence.example: Augustus settledOn Nicopolis, time -0030/-0029.

shape.basis: Settling veterans on land is an act of distribution.
shape.by: Claude (proposed under D-138, 2026-11-12; for the curator to confirm)

requests.name: sparedBy
definitions: A defeated person is pardoned or preserved unharmed by the victor at a given date.

evidence.example: Gaius Sosius sparedBy Augustus, 31 BCE

shape.basis: Sparing is an act (the same as clemency granted, seen from the other side).
shape.by: Claude (proposed under D-138, 2026-11-12; for the curator to confirm)

requests.name: struckCoinage
definitions: A person or authority issued a coin type at a given time.

evidence.example: Mark Antony struckCoinage legionary denarii, time -0032/-0031 (RRC 544, not held).

shape.basis: An issue of coins is an act: who struck it, where, when (or a Work/Object claim).
shape.by: Claude (proposed under D-138, 2026-11-12; for the curator to confirm)

requests.name: surrenderedTo
definitions: A force or person yielded to an enemy commander at a stated date.

evidence.example: Antony's land army surrenderedTo Augustus, September 31 BCE, some days after the battle

shape.basis: A surrender happens at a moment (the army's surrender is already a phase).
shape.by: Claude (proposed under D-138, 2026-11-12; for the curator to confirm)

requests.name: sworeAllegianceTo
definitions: A community or group takes an oath of loyalty to a person at a date.

evidence.example: Italy sworeAllegianceTo Augustus (coniuratio Italiae), 32 BCE

shape.basis: An oath is sworn at a moment.
shape.by: Claude (proposed under D-138, 2026-11-12; for the curator to confirm)

requests.name: transportedTreasure
definitions: A person or group carried a treasury or store of valuables from one place to another at a given time.

evidence.example: Cleopatra's squadron at Actium transportedTreasure to Alexandria, time -0030-09-02 (c208).

shape.basis: Moving treasure is an act with a time and route.
shape.by: Claude (proposed under D-138, 2026-11-12; for the curator to confirm)

requests.name: vetoed
definitions: An act: a tribune (or a colleague) blocked a proposal, a decree or an act of a magistrate by intercessio, at a date; the vetoer and the measure are roles.

evidence.ref: chats/Agents and Exploration.yml (ChatGPT review of the architecture, 2026-11-21); 39 §10, the families the lens run and the Gracchus narrative ask for. The objectKinds Law and Decree wait on registry v21 (D-171; 48 §4). A vetoed Senate motion is recorded as a senatus auctoritas, the vote's outcome.

shape.basis: A veto is an act at a moment against a named measure: an Event with roles (D-138).
shape.by: curator, 2026-11-22 (48 §3, confirmed in chat)

requests.name: wentOverTo
definitions: A force or its members defected or surrendered to another person or force.

evidence.quotation: they went over to the conqueror
Amyntas and Deiotarus went over to Caesar
they went over to the conqueror

shape.basis: The same act as defectedTo: a desertion is an event.
shape.by: Claude (proposed under D-138, 2026-11-12; for the curator to confirm)
